kind: pre-fit declaration (registration_protocol.md section 2, steps 1 and 3) with a resolvability gate
written_by: mandate-maps worker, RAF round, 9 October 2026 (owner-approved step)
written_before: any view of the Palestine Open Maps 'Aerial imagery, 1940s' layer anywhere

registered_prediction.copied_from: research/assessments/kohlit_chain/chain.json (sha256 above), model M-SULTAN, next link SULTAN-1-precamp-mouth
registered_prediction.expect: A non-funerary opening (shaft, cistern or pit mouth, 1 m or wider) with at least one grave cut or tomb opening within 10 m of it.
registered_prediction.where: The strip from the tell's north foot to about 250 m north: Kenyon II p. 169 skipped it; Area D lies about 100–200 m north (Fig. 91, inference). Under the ʿAin es-Sultan camp since 1948.
registered_prediction.success: The opening and the grave appear in one registered record, and their distance is 'inside' 10 m under registration_protocol.md.
registered_prediction.contradiction: Photographs and plans alone cannot contradict: absence may be concealment, burial or resolution. A contradiction needs a coverage-gated excavation record of the strip (coverage module gates) that reached the ancient surface and reports no such pair.
registered_prediction.notes: Locating an opening does not date it. A success opens the next link (R-E60-PIT-PERIOD, R-E60-JOINT-ACCESS) on the same feature.

record_specific_expectation: The layer's maximum zoom is 16, about 2.03 m per ground pixel. A 1 m opening would span about half a pixel. The resolvability gate below is therefore expected to fail, in which case the strip stays unseen and SULTAN-1 stays untested by this record.

document.title: RAF vertical photographs of the 1940s as a georeferenced mosaic (S. Holtzman), Palestine Open Maps layer 'Aerial imagery, 1940s', zoom 16, around Tell es-Sultan
document.custodian: Palestine Open Maps (tiles on jsDelivr from github.com/bothness/pom-tiles); photographs credited to the RAF and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem
document.date: 1944-1948 per the layer; sortie and frame not stated (catalogue: PS30 15 Mar 1945, PS32 16 Apr 1945 cover the tell)
document.kind: vertical_aerial (a resampled mosaic of near-vertical photographs)
document.extent_grid: EPSG:28191 E 189500-194500, N 140000-145000 (zoom-16 tiles intersecting the box)
document.sha256: SHA-256 of the sorted tile manifest (z/x/y and each tile's SHA-256), computed at download and written into the pre-preview note before any view

transform_note: Section 3: near-vertical photograph; plain-level points only. Mound tops and Jebel Quruntul are excluded.
source_axes: pixel_y_down (pixels of the full-resolution zoom-16 mosaic of the extent; x and y measured from its top-left global pixel)

target_frame.crs: EPSG:28191 Palestine Grid metres (= WBADB Old Israel Grid minus 1,000,000 m N)
target_frame.reference_source: The Esri World Imagery coordinates already fixed in registrations/POM-pal20k-z16-19-14.json (picked before this layer was viewed). They are reused unchanged.

control_candidates: RP-TELL-FOOT-E (only if the spring is identifiable, because its line runs through the spring)

excluded_candidates.RP-SAMARAT: no reference coordinate (no mound identifiable on the reference imagery)
excluded_candidates.RP-TELL-FOOT-N: excluded by role; inside the mask

control_rule: Use every candidate the photograph shows with a definable point outside the mask, at the point defined in reference_points.json and picked by the same definition as on the reference imagery. At least three. A candidate is dropped only if its feature cannot be identified on the photograph; that is decided before any fit.
check_point_rule: RP-SPRING if the coarse masked preview shows the spring house or the reservoir outside the mask. Otherwise the first identifiable of RP-TELL-FOOT-W, RP-TELL-FOOT-S. Decided on the coarse preview and written down before any full-resolution view.

zone_and_mask.coarse_preview_mask: mask_grid widened by 150 m west, east and north and 50 m south (no layer offset is known yet): E 191650-192700, N 142070-142850; painted solid before downsampling to 8 m per pixel
zone_and_mask.full_resolution_mask: mask_grid shifted by the layer offset measured on the coarse preview from features outside the zone, widened by 75 m west, east and north and 50 m south; written into the checkpoint note before any full-resolution view
zone_and_mask.stricter_than_protocol: The zone is painted solid on every view, not only marked.

resolvability_gate.declared: before any view of the layer; applies before the zone may be opened at full resolution
resolvability_gate.measure: Effective ground resolution R_eff on features OUTSIDE the zone = the larger of (a) the nominal ground pixel of the highest available zoom and (b) the median 10-90 % edge-rise width, in metres, of at least three sharp straight edges (road margins, walls, building or reservoir edges) on full-resolution masked views.
resolvability_gate.rule: Pass only if R_eff <= 0.5 m, so that a 1 m opening spans at least about 2 pixels. If it fails: do not open the zone at full resolution; keep the zone unseen; report that the 600-dpi Hebrew University scans (PS30 5107, PS30 5137, PS32 5069-5070; record REC-RAF-JERICHO) are needed.
resolvability_gate.fit_if_failed: The registration fit may still be run on points outside the zone, to record this layer's registration error. It opens nothing inside the mask.

no_rescue: Controls, transform, check point and gate are fixed before the fit and before any zone view. A later change is a new exploratory registration and is logged as such.
